speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to help me narrow down the cause, have you noticed any hearing loss, tinnitus, or ringing in your ear alongside the spinning sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

Given the sudden onset lasting only 3 minutes and the immediate return to baseline, this clinical picture strongly suggests BPPV rather than vestibular neuritis or Meniere's disease. Did you notice that the spinning sensation was triggered specifically by changing your head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up?
